report.summary: One action-required stale assertion: the threat model still claims bcrypt at cost 12, while password hashing now uses Argon2id.

findings.title: Password-hashing assertion still claims bcrypt after migration to Argon2id

model_excerpt.quote: An attacker who obtains the users table cracks password hashes offline. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt at cost 12 in internal/auth/password.go, which keeps offline cracking expensive.

evidence.note: The password implementation now imports golang.org/x/crypto/argon2 rather than bcrypt.
HashPassword derives stored hashes with Argon2id using parameters 1, 64*1024 KiB, 4 threads, and a 32-byte output.
VerifyPassword also derives the candidate hash with Argon2id, confirming bcrypt verification is no longer used.

relevance.justification: The changed implementation directly contradicts the model's specific claim that password.go uses bcrypt at cost 12.

findings.agent_prompt: Update app.tm.hcl, threat "credential database theft" at line 12: replace the claim that internal/auth/password.go uses bcrypt at cost 12 with an accurate description of the new Argon2id implementation and its parameters (1 iteration, 64 MiB memory, 4 threads, 32-byte key, and a random 16-byte salt). The implementation changed to argon2.IDKey at internal/auth/password.go:18 and :37. Keep control "password hashing" implemented=true because server-side password hashing remains present.
findings.suggested_fix: Revise the credential-database-theft threat description to document Argon2id and its current salt and work-factor parameters instead of bcrypt cost 12.
